PullRequest.Title: chat: add a developer command to simulate a Copilot plan
PullRequest.Body:
Adds a **Developer: Simulate Copilot Plan...** command to try the product as a user with a different Copilot plan, in particular a signed-in user who can claim Copilot Free but has not signed up yet. This makes it possible to build and test experiences for such users without a matching account.

### What changed

- The quick pick offers: Actual Plan / Stop Simulating, Can Claim Copilot Free, No Copilot Access, Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise.
- While a plan is simulated, a status bar entry shows `Simulating: <plan>`. Clicking it reopens the picker to switch plans or stop. Changes apply immediately without a reload and persist across reloads (profile-scoped).
- The simulation substitutes the entitlements data *before* it is mapped to a `ChatEntitlement`, so the plan, SKU, quotas, context keys, setup flow, status bar and dashboard all follow it. Account identity (organisations, staff flag, tracking ID) is kept so internal-user checks keep working. The SKU/plan mapping was extracted into `getChatEntitlement` without behavior changes.

### Safety

- Signing up while simulating never contacts GitHub, including on retries. It switches the simulation to Copilot Free instead.
- Quotas pushed from the Copilot extension or the agent host are ignored while simulating, and quotas are cleared whenever the simulation changes, so actual and simulated snapshots are never merged.
- `chatInstallEntitlement`, `chatEntitlements` and the additional-spend events are not sent while simulating.
- Nothing changes when no simulation is active.

### Known limitations

- The Copilot extension keeps its own token, so chat requests still use the actual account. Everything driven by the workbench entitlement state follows the simulation.
- Events that read the current SKU, such as `interactiveSessionProviderInvoked.requestStartCopilotSku`, report the simulated value while a simulation is active.

### How to test

1. Sign in with GitHub and run **Developer: Simulate Copilot Plan...**.
2. Pick **Can Claim Copilot Free**. The status bar shows the simulation and the Copilot entry offers setup. Choosing **Use AI Features** moves the simulation to Copilot Free without contacting GitHub.
3. Reload the window. The simulation is still active.
4. Click the status bar entry and choose **Stop Simulating**. The actual plan and quotas return without a reload.

### Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatEntitlementService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSetupController.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSetup/chatSetup.test.ts`: 68 passing
- Manually verified in Code OSS: simulating Can Claim Copilot Free, simulated sign-up, persistence across reloads, switching plans from the status bar entry, and stopping the simulation. The final review fixes (sign-up retry guard, quota reset, profile scope, telemetry suppression) were covered by the type check and unit tests, not by another manual run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal window startup with no simulated entitlement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatSetupContribution already dereferences ChatEntitlementService.context and requests during BlockRestore before this diff's AfterRestored contribution runs. The added contribution only reads the already-created request controller, checks one cached profile-storage value, and registers a listener; no new work must complete before restore.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the profile-scoped simulated-entitlement key through IStorageService's cached synchronous API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional keyed read per request-controller construction, plus bounded reads on entitlement-context telemetry updates; effective cardinality is one controller per window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request controller was already eagerly constructed by ChatSetupContribution, but did not read this simulation key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The constructor read occurs during the pre-existing BlockRestore initialization of ChatEntitlementRequests, but the storage service read is from its loaded cache and does not add a disk request on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Default-account entitlement/provider refresh transitively supplies the account consumed by ChatEntitlementRequests.resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional request from this diff; getDefaultAccount waits for the provider's existing initialization and the request controller was already created by ChatSetupContribution before the new contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ChatSetupContribution already dereferenced requests.value at BlockRestore, causing the same resolve path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not moved onto the startup path by this diff and not awaited by the new AfterRestored contribution constructor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same as before when simulation is inactive; zero while simulation is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Telemetry was emitted on context updates regardless of simulation, which did not previously exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry remains off the product critical path, and the diff suppresses rather than adds transmission during simulation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One window and one entitlement controller; repeated work scales only with infrequent entitlement/context changes, not editor input, frames, rows, or chat messages.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One controller resolve per window; pre-existing cancellation replaces an older resolve. The new status contribution does not launch another resolve.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The simulation key is read from IStorageService's already-loaded profile cache. Default-account initialization and entitlement data retain their pre-diff caching and coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the BlockRestore constructor and request-controller call path that no expensive boundary was newly introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact synchronous storage lookup cost is unmeasured, but it is a bounded cached key lookup and does not establish a reportable startup regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: normal startup adds only bounded cached-key/listener work, while the potentially expensive entitlement initialization was already on an earlier startup phase.

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer selects, switches, or stops a simulated Copilot plan
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker waits for one profile-storage store/remove and one local entitlement recomputation before announcing completion. The recomputation consumes the current default account and synthesized quota objects; it does not refresh the account or issue an entitlement request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist or remove the profile-scoped simulated entitlement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One keyed write per accepted picker change, fanned out once to each open window sharing the profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No simulation state was persisted because the developer feature did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initiating action awaits the resulting local resolve before its ARIA announcement; the write is bounded and explicitly required for persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the current default account before locally mapping simulated entitlement data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getDefaultAccount call per effective simulation change per open window; this waits for existing initialization and performs no refresh itself.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no simulation-change scenario; ordinary entitlement refresh uses refresh/forceResolve paths rather than this local storage event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The local resolve is awaited by the initiating picker action, but no network fetch is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Nine fixed picker options; one selected value. Cross-window fanout scales with the small number of concurrently open windows, not repository or user data size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each window handles the storage event independently. Within a window, resolve cancels its predecessor; picker invocation awaits the latest stored-change resolve.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Actual account data is reused from DefaultAccountService; no cold network fetch is requested. Duplicate local and storage events are coalesced by comparing the stored value with _simulatedEntitlement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that persistence and fanout are real and that account/network refresh is absent from getDefaultAccount on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cross-window count varies by user, but this is an explicitly invoked developer command with bounded local work per window.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new work is bounded, user-triggered, coalesced for duplicate notifications, and does not fan out across data items or remote calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Quota snapshots arrive while a plan is simulated
Scenarios.CriticalPath: acceptQuotas checks the already-instantiated request controller and returns before quota merging, context-key updates, storage writes, event fanout, and telemetry. Simulated quotas are applied only by the local resolve through doAcceptQuotas.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Process extension or agent-host quota snapshot delivery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One constant-time simulation-state check per incoming snapshot; expensive downstream work is skipped while simulation is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every incoming snapshot proceeded through merging, context updates, possible profile-storage writes, events, and telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff reduces work on the snapshot delivery path and keeps simulated state stable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit additional-spend telemetry after quota changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged when simulation is inactive; zero while simulation is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible quota transitions could emit telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suppressed after local state updates during simulation; no new boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with quota snapshot frequency, but the added check is constant time and prevents larger work while active.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Incoming snapshots are synchronously rejected while simulation is active; no queued or burst remote work is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Actual and simulated quota snapshots are deliberately not merged; clearing and one local replacement occur on each effective simulation change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the early return and direct doAcceptQuotas path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Snapshot frequency is environment-dependent, but the direction of performance change is neutral to beneficial.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the changed mechanism removes repeated work and telemetry rather than regressing performance.

Scenarios.Scenario: User invokes Copilot Free sign-up while simulation is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The sign-up path switches the stored simulated entitlement to Free and waits for the local resolve. It returns before session iteration and the HTTP POST/retry path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST Copilot Free sign-up for authentication sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero while simulated; ordinary non-simulated behavior retains up to one request per candidate session per retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The ordinary sign-up path contacted the configured entitlement endpoint; there was no simulated-sign-up scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes the remote boundary from the simulated sign-up path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One keyed profile write if the simulation changes to Free; duplicate Free selection is coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited locally, replacing a much slower network sign-up boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed one entitlement transition; remote session cardinality is eliminated on this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One local entitlement resolve per effective transition; prior resolve is canceled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the current default-account data and storage cache; no negative-cache or retry loop is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the early simulation guard before request construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to regression assessment; the path strictly removes remote work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: simulated sign-up is a bounded local replacement for the existing network/retry path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup initialization, simulation persistence and cross-window fanout, quota delivery, telemetry, status-bar lifecycle, and simulated sign-up. The only newly eager work is bounded cached storage/listener setup; existing BlockRestore code already constructs the entitlement request controller. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
